_comment: THE canonical feature list. Every user-visible capability of Ergopti+ has
exactly one name here, and every driver either implements it under that name
or does not implement it at all — never under a second spelling.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the list lived in prose in TODO.md, so nothing could
read it. Invariant I1 ('one tree') and Convention S ('the stub with a
reason') both need a machine-readable canonical list, and without one the
tree-parity gate could only compare the drivers to EACH OTHER — which says
nothing about a feature none of them has, and cannot tell a deliberate
THE `tree` FIELD IS NOT DECORATION, and writing this file is what made that
clear. The prose list said every named feature is `modules/<name>/`. The tree
disagrees, and the tree is right: a feature the user OPERATES lives in
modules/ (gestures, llm, shortcuts), while a feature the user LOOKS AT is a
window and lives in ui/ (action_picker, changelog, model_browser). Ten of the
25 are windows. Forcing them into modules/ would have been a rename in
HOW TO USE IT: test-driver-tree-parity.cjs reads it and ratchets how many
canonical features are present on all three drivers. Add a feature here when
it gains a name a user could say out loud, not when a folder appears.

features.name: action_picker
features.role: picker window for gesture and chord actions

features.name: diagnostics
features.role: crash reporting and the diagnostic dump

features.name: download_window
features.role: asset and model downloads with progress

features.name: gestures
features.role: trackpad gesture slots and their actions

features.name: healthcheck
features.role: the health window and its probes

features.name: layout
features.role: the physical keyboard layout and its install

features.name: keylogger
features.role: keystroke capture and its aggregates — the menu calls it Metrics

features.name: paths
features.role: resolution of every user file location

features.name: personal_info_editor
features.role: the user's own data for dynamic expansions

features.name: shortcuts
features.role: chords, text transforms and their bindings

_absent_everywhere: CORRECTED TWICE, AND THE SECOND PASS FOUND THE SAME MISTAKE AS THE FIRST.
This list named six entries as absent from every driver, then four. Of the
four, only ONE was really absent everywhere. The rest were this file
describing the drivers wrongly — the identical failure that produced the
first correction, so it is worth stating as a rule: before treating an
absence as work, open the three drivers and find where the capability
actually lives. It has been somewhere every single time.
CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (first pass): personal_info is ui/personal_info_editor
and hotstrings_config is ui/hotstrings_config_window, both present on all
three. The canonical entry simply used a shorter name than the folder every
driver ships. Count 14 -> 16, no driver code touched.
CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (second pass), entry by entry:
download — WAS `modules/download`, NOW `ui/download_window`. Wrong tree by
this file's own rule at the top: a feature the user LOOKS AT is a window
and lives in ui/. macOS and Linux both ship ui/download_window, so the
entry was reported as absent everywhere while two drivers had it under the
name it should always have carried. It is now a 2-of-3 partial, which is
the truth. The previous note called Windows's absence 'a genuine 2-of-3 gap
rather than a naming one'; the path half is right and the second half is
not. Windows ships modules/llm/ollama_webview.ahk, 532 lines, loading the
SAME _shared/ui/download_window/index.html at the same 460x380 geometry. Its
display API has zero live callers — the module went dormant when the install
moved to winget, and tests/meta/test_ollama_webview_msgsub_retained.ahk
records that as a deliberate, maintained state rather than an oversight. So
Windows has the capability, at a different path, switched off on purpose.
Also worth knowing before anyone consolidates the three: Linux's is a
78-line stub whose cancel and retry return success without acting.
layout — GENUINELY SPREAD, and it is not going to become one folder. Windows
emulates the layout in software (modules/keymap/layout.ahk plus three files,
~2 050 lines) and has no install path at all. macOS installs a real keyboard
layout and switches input sources (modules/keymap/layout{,_install}.lua,
input_sources.lua, ~1 390 lines). Linux ships the Ergopti->QWERTY table as
DATA inside platform/remap/data/kanata.kbd and has nothing to install,
because kanata reads the file. Three drivers, three different meanings of
'install', and platform/remap is NOT the shared home it looks like — that
directory is the remap ENGINE (tap-holds on Windows, Karabiner on macOS,
the kanata daemon on Linux), a different capability that happens to sit
next to this one on one driver.
apps — FOUR MEANINGS UNDER ONE WORD, which is why no folder can hold it.
(1) per-app LLM profile overrides, a Windows-only feature the generated
manifests mark platforms = { "ahk" }; (2) per-app exclusion lists, whose two
consumers persist to different config sections (llm.trigger/disabled_apps
against metrics/metrics_disabled_apps); (3) app -> category mapping for the
metrics aggregates; and (4) on macOS, a top-level apps/ folder of bundled
.app utilities, which means 'applications' in an unrelated sense. Creating
modules/apps/ would satisfy the gate and make the tree harder to read.
metrics — WAS `modules/metrics`, NOW `modules/keylogger`, which all three
drivers already ship. Renaming the FOLDERS to metrics was considered and
rejected, and the reason generalises: 295 tracked files reference
modules/keylogger (macOS 137, Windows 115, Linux 20, tools 10, docs 8),
including three cross-driver JS gates that pin the path as a string and
would fail at runtime rather than at review. Worse, moving only the folder
is a HALF rename — keylogger.lua, the [keylogger] log tags and
KEYLOGGER_SPEC.md would all still say keylogger inside a folder called
metrics, which is the two-spellings problem this list exists to remove,
relocated. And it would invert the lesson this file has now recorded three
times: the drivers agreed with each other and only the list disagreed.
'Metrics' stays the word the user reads in the menu; 'keylogger' is the
word the code uses for the module that captures the keystrokes. A canonical
entry names a folder, not a label — infra/paths and modules/diagnostics are
not phrases a user says either.
